item.content:encoded:
I'm kind of feeling that one of the reasons this anomaly is dangerous is exactly because it's not perceived as dangerous - merely annoying. That's the kind of thing that can make you lower your guard, think "well, it's at least super obvious where it passes through. It just requires some cleanup afterwards."

Call me paranoid but I could imagine that as a false trail, where the entity intentionally acts as obnoxiously as possible in some highly visible places to divert attention from other instances of 732 where the edits are much harder to tell apart from the genuine report. The containment protocols are essential to the foundation: imagine the chaos if 732 managed to slip in an edit that compromised containment for a keter? Imagine if it manage to slip in several such edits and the following events cascade into multiple containment breaches - it could possibly singlehandedly decommission entire facilities and potentially shuffle the blame to foundation personnel.

Or it's just a really immature AI and I'm reading too much into it.

item.title: this was nearly a down-vote from me.
item.content:encoded:
Honestly. First read I could almost taste my disgust at it. So like, superficial and, like all casual…felt like I had accidentally clicked onto 4chan.

Then I though about this thing spreading, becoming much more sophisticated and evolving…
This evening, I find myself sitting in front of a TV programme that is reviewing genuine medical news headlines of 2016. Here are a few examples;

"Studies find that Facebook users are less likely to die."
"Everything you use or consume is almost 100% likely to be a carcinogen."
"Paracetamol makes you into a sociopath."
"A box that generates EMPF cures many diseases, including cancer."

Some of these may seem heavily paraphrased, not by much to be honest.
Now I find myself not laughing, getting angry, or getting irritated by SCP-732.
I find myself getting rather frightened.

When I first read it, I would have never seen that coming.

item.title: Theories
item.content:encoded:
My caffeine-infused mind seems to be on a roll tonight. SCP-732 is probably one of the below:

  • It is an entity that turns documents into stereotypically bad fanfiction (like "My Immortal"; God bless the souls of all who've read it).
  • It is a memetic 'virus' that infects the minds of people with unusually strong obsessions. The virus may or may not compel the infected to write terrible fanfiction.
  • It's both; a mind-affecting entity that does exactly what I just said it might do.

Either way (or not), it's an upvote for me.

item.content:encoded:
I'm agreeing with those above: this fails in that it doesn't read anything like actual fanfiction.

This article would also be better if, instead of the word 'deployment", it said "creation".

EDIT: To explain a little further, I think this has two angles going for it: the idea of an anomalous virus wiping out information, and the satirical element parodying SCP fanfiction. It definitely fails on the second count, because nobody writes like that. Fanfiction is typically poorly-proofread, but the SCP effect reads entirely like this:

TEH HOROR!!!1!!11!! TEH ELdRICH HOROR!!!11!!!!11!!

which is completely overwrought even by the standards of intentionally bad writing. And the first angle fails for me for the same reason: it's just turning data into gibberish. Plenty of viruses do that already.

This would work for me if it actually managed to be a little convincing. You could tell which parts were falsified if you were paying attentionthere would just be seamless transitions into outrageous lies and back again. The idea that something out there might be gradually making records more ludicrous when nobody's looking would actually be a little frighteningand it would explain a lot, besides.

item.content:encoded:
Upvoted, even though the article is a little silly. That said, I take a bit of issue with the title. As an avid and prolific writer of fanfiction myself, I'm somewhat offended by the implication that fanfiction is deliberately written with misspellings, grammatical errors, and leet. Even the qualifying term I've seen people use here in the discussion page ("bad" fanfiction) points a jab directly at fanfiction and fanfiction alone. This is not "bad fanfiction", this is "bad writing".

Fanfiction writing is just as legitimate of an art form as regular fiction writing is. I'm sure there are fanfics written with the idiotic format demonstrated by this SCP, but even if that's the case, such written pieces are not written like that because they're fanfiction. Maybe it's (arguably) a little easier for idiots to write fanfiction than it is for them to write regular fiction, but it's still a matter of the poor writing of individual authors, not the genre as a whole.

That is all.
